register: wave-9 authoring register (S-B9 tranche) — part 2 of 2

items.stem: Define substitution in one sentence.
items.modelAnswer: Substitution happens when one atom or functional group in a molecule is replaced by another.

items.stem: State what distinguishes an addition reaction from every other reaction type at this level.
items.modelAnswer: Two or more molecules combine into a single larger product, with no other products formed.

items.stem: Both the methane-bromine and the ethene-bromine reactions consume one Br2 molecule. Explain why the first needs ultraviolet light while the second does not.
items.modelAnswer: Methane is a saturated alkane, so swapping a halogen for a hydrogen is substitution and only proceeds under UV radiation; ethene is an alkene whose C=C opens by addition, a move that needs no UV condition.

items.stem: Ethene is reacted with hydrogen bromide, HBr. State how many products form and classify the reaction.
items.modelAnswer: Addition: the molecules combine into the single larger product bromoethane, so just one product forms.

items.stem: State the two products of the complete combustion of any hydrocarbon.
items.modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide and water, formed when air or oxygen is in unlimited supply.

items.stem: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of propane.
Explain why a blue flame differs from a yellow, sooty flame in terms of the oxygen available and the carbon product.
items.modelAnswer: A blue flame has plenty of oxygen, so the carbon leaves as carbon dioxide; a yellow, sooty flame is oxygen-starved, so incomplete combustion gives carbon monoxide and carbon soot instead.

items.stem: A Bunsen burner's air hole is slowly closed. State what happens to the flame colour and name the carbon-containing products that begin to appear.
items.modelAnswer: The flame turns yellow and luminous as incomplete combustion sets in, producing carbon monoxide and carbon soot alongside water.

items.stem: State the condition without which an alkane ignores a halogen.
items.modelAnswer: Ultraviolet radiation (UV light) must be present for the reaction to occur.

items.stem: Give the two products when methane reacts with chlorine under UV light.
items.modelAnswer: Chloromethane, CH3Cl, and hydrogen chloride, HCl.

items.stem: Explain why the methane-bromine reaction is classified as substitution rather than addition.
items.modelAnswer: A bromine atom replaces one hydrogen atom of methane, giving CH3Br and HBr; nothing adds across a bond and the two bromine atoms end up in different molecules, which is why the move is substitution and not addition.

items.stem: Methane is brominated under UV in a shortage of bromine. State why the mixture contains no doubly-brominated product.
items.modelAnswer: The reaction is limited to mono-substitution: only one halogen atom replaces a hydrogen per methane molecule, so no dibrominated product forms.

items.stem: What generic family name covers organic molecules that carry a halogen atom?
items.modelAnswer: They are called halogenoalkanes, or haloalkanes for short.

items.stem: List four uses of halogenoalkanes.
items.modelAnswer: Solvents, refrigerants, propellants and pharmaceuticals.

items.stem: Explain why CFC refrigerants were withdrawn even though they performed well.
items.modelAnswer: CFCs are chlorofluorocarbons that harm the ozone layer, so the whole family was phased out despite its usefulness.

items.stem: A workshop needs a degreasing fluid and picks a solvent made by the UV substitution route. Write the equation for making it from methane and chlorine.
items.modelAnswer: CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl, run under ultraviolet light.

items.stem: Give the number of carbon atoms signalled by the stem hex.
items.modelAnswer: Hex counts six carbon atoms.

items.stem: Name the suffix that signals an O-H group on the chain.
items.modelAnswer: The suffix -anol marks the alcohol family, as in methanol.

items.stem: Explain how the name methanol tells you both the chain length and the family of the molecule.
items.modelAnswer: The stem meth counts one carbon atom and the suffix -anol shows the alcohol group, so the single name encodes both facts at once.

items.stem: An unknown straight-chain molecule has six carbons and one C=C bond. Write its name.
items.modelAnswer: Hexene - hex for the six carbons, -ene for the double bond.

items.stem: State the prefix used when a molecule carries two of the same functional group.
items.modelAnswer: The prefix di- is attached to the second part of the name for two identical groups.

items.stem: What job do the numbers in an organic name do?
items.modelAnswer: They give the position of the functional group or side chain along the carbon chain.

items.stem: Explain how the naming rules separate two isomers that share one molecular formula.
items.modelAnswer: The same rules are applied to each different structure in turn, so every isomer receives a name that reflects its own arrangement of atoms.

items.stem: A name reads 2-chlorobutane. State how many carbons the chain has and what sits on carbon number 2.
items.modelAnswer: But counts four carbons, and the 2 says a chlorine atom (the chloro group) sits on carbon number 2.

items.stem: Define the word fuel.
items.modelAnswer: A fuel is a substance that releases heat energy when it burns - an exothermic change.

items.stem: Name the three main fossil fuels and state what they all are in terms of supply.
items.modelAnswer: Coal, oil (crude oil) and natural gas - and all of them are finite resources.

items.stem: Explain why no fossil fuel can burn without an acid-rain implication.
items.modelAnswer: Every fossil fuel contains small amounts of sulfur impurities alongside its carbon and hydrogen, and those impurities burn to sulfur dioxide, the gas that dissolves in raindrops to make acid rain.

items.stem: A camp stove burns butane, C4H10, in plenty of air. Deduce the balanced equation for its complete combustion.
List the three products of incomplete combustion.
items.modelAnswer: Unburnt fuel as soot, carbon monoxide and water.

items.stem: Write the balanced equation for methane burning in a limited oxygen supply to give carbon monoxide.
Explain why a boiler running in a closed room is where incomplete combustion is most likely to strike.
items.modelAnswer: A closed room runs short of air, so the flame receives insufficient oxygen - exactly the condition that forces incomplete combustion instead of the complete burning the appliance was designed for.

items.stem: A methane flame in very poor air leaves a black layer on a cold pan. Write the equation the note gives for this outcome and name the black deposit.
items.modelAnswer: CH4 + O2 -> C + 2H2O; the black deposit is carbon soot.

items.stem: State the three sensory properties of carbon monoxide that make it so dangerous indoors.
items.modelAnswer: It is odourless, colourless and tasteless, so it can be inhaled without being noticed.

items.stem: State how many times more strongly haemoglobin binds carbon monoxide than oxygen.
items.modelAnswer: Around 200 to 250 times more strongly, forming stable carboxyhaemoglobin.

items.stem: Explain why inhaled carbon monoxide reduces the oxygen reaching the body's tissues.
items.modelAnswer: The CO is absorbed into the red blood cells and binds tightly to the molecules that normally carry oxygen, cutting the capacity of the blood to transport oxygen round the body.

items.stem: A family lights a charcoal heater inside a sealed tent and dizziness soon sets in. State which gas is responsible and why the tent's confinement matters.
items.modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide from the incomplete burning of the charcoal is responsible: it binds to the blood's oxygen carriers, and the sealed tent keeps oxygen scarce so the incomplete combustion - and the CO - keep building.

items.stem: State the definition of a hydrocarbon.
items.modelAnswer: A compound whose molecules contain hydrogen and carbon atoms and no other element - only those two.

items.stem: Name two carbon compounds that are excluded from organic chemistry by convention.
items.modelAnswer: Metal carbonates, carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide are the conventional exclusions - any two of them.

items.stem: Explain why ethanol, which contains oxygen, cannot be called a hydrocarbon.
items.modelAnswer: The hydrocarbon rule admits hydrogen and carbon only; any other element present - here oxygen - disqualifies the molecule.

items.stem: A fuel supplier lists natural gas as its product. State which hydrocarbon dominates natural gas and why hydrocarbons matter commercially.
items.modelAnswer: Natural gas consists mainly of methane, and hydrocarbons matter because fuels such as petrol and natural gas are built from them.

items.stem: What does an empirical formula give you about the atoms in a molecule?
items.modelAnswer: The simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms in a molecule.

items.stem: Which of the five formula types would you draw to display every single bond explicitly?
items.modelAnswer: The displayed formula, which shows every atom and every bond including their spatial arrangement.

items.stem: Explain the difference in job between a molecular formula and a general formula.
items.modelAnswer: A molecular formula counts the actual atoms in one molecule, while a general formula carrying the letter n describes a whole family of compounds at once.

items.stem: A hydrocarbon sample is found to contain molecules of C4H10 exactly. State its empirical formula.
items.modelAnswer: Dividing every subscript by 2, the simplest whole-number ratio is C2H5.

items.stem: State the two things every member of a homologous series shares.
items.modelAnswer: The same functional group and similar chemical properties.

items.stem: State the fixed difference between neighbouring members of a homologous series.
items.modelAnswer: They differ by one CH2 unit between neighbours.

items.stem: Explain what gradation means down a homologous series, giving one property that shows it.
items.modelAnswer: Physical properties change gradually as the chains grow longer - for example the boiling point rises member by member instead of jumping.

items.stem: Propene and cyclopropane share one molecular formula. State that formula and the name of the relationship between the two molecules.
items.modelAnswer: Both are C3H6; sharing the molecular formula but differing in their displayed formulae makes them isomers.
